runners_data.name: Esdaile
runners_data.spotlight: 15,000gns foal; by Oasis Dream; fifth foal; half-sister to 1m2f-1m4f winner Jawhary (RPR 82); dam unraced sister to 1m 2yo Group 3 winner Helleborine (dam of good sprinter Calyx) and 6f Group 1 winner African Rose; she has a useful standard to aim at and likely best watched.

runners_data.name: Kino Plasmat
runners_data.spotlight: 250,000gns foal; eighth foal; Wootton Basset half-sister to winners Waikuku (7f-1m1f including multiple HK Group 1s; RPR 124), Waipiro (1m2f including Group 3; 113), It's Good To Laugh (7.3f 2yo/1m4f Flat, 99; 2m-2m3f hurdle) and Dancing Rebel (5f 2yo; 84); dam placed 7f (72); lots to like on paper and he is one to note for market confidence.

runners_data.name: La Mariposa
runners_data.comment: By Zoustar; dam 7f/1m winner (93); unlikely newcomer but market check advised
runners_data.spotlight: 40-1 when a tailed-off last of five on her Newmarket debut eight weeks ago (7f, good); longer-term prospect.

runners_data.name: Starlight Lass
runners_data.spotlight: By Dubawi; first foal of a 1m 2yo winner (RPR 90), herself a half-sister to St Leger winner Logician; stable won the corresponding event last year but with a filly who had experience; betting instructive.

runners_data.name: Sugar Sugar
runners_data.spotlight: Tenth foal; half-sister to five winners including The Night Porter (7f-1m2f including Hong Kong; RPR 95), Wonderful World (6f 2yo; 87) and Dancin Boy (1m-1m2f including Switzerland; 84); dam 7f winner (72), half-sister Irish 1,000 Guineas winner Samitar; apprentice-ridden and sports headgear on debut.

runners_data.name: Yimmna
runners_data.spotlight: 650,000euros yearling by Siyouni; second foal; half-sister to French 9.5f AW/1m2f turf winner Audubon Park (including Listed; RPR 112); dam placed 1m-9.5f in France, half-sister to French 1m4f Group 1 winner Left Hand; lots to like on paper and William Haggas won this race in 2022 (with a newcomer) and 2023; high on the list.

runners_data.name: Quadrillion
runners_data.spotlight: Top-class pedigree and she made a promising start to her career when third of six in a fillies' novice at Newmarket last July (7f, good to firm); odds-on favourite for a Leicester novice one month later when soundly beaten into second but the winner on that occasion is now BHA-rated 112 and finished fifth in the Irish 2000 Guineas; capable of better and she is a strong contender back from a break.

runners_data.name: Shushu
runners_data.comment: From respected Newmarket yard & bred to have bright future; she's one to consider on debut
runners_data.spotlight: Solid start to her career when second of five behind a good prospect at Haydock three weeks ago (7f, soft); open to improvement but may not come into her own until tackling 1m+.

runners_data.name: Victorian Rose
runners_data.comment: Victor Ludorum filly; the betting should prove an accurate indicator for this newcomer
runners_data.spotlight: 80-1 and well beaten on Kempton debut three weeks ago (7f); hard to recommend.

runners_data.name: Sterling Fortune
runners_data.spotlight: Never the slightest threat on her Kempton debut five weeks ago (7f, AW) but only one of the other 13 runners covered the final furlong faster; should do better at some point.

runners_data.name: Too Too Divine
runners_data.comment: Last of four in one AW race; could be a big improver this season, which she needs to be
runners_data.spotlight: Modest form in her two 7f runs, the second of them over C&D six weeks ago (good to firm); might find life easier once handicapping.

runners_data.name: Komodo Rose

runners_data.name: Blindfold Games

runners_data.name: Miss Starlet
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose form has declined in handicaps, needs to reverse recent trend
runners_data.comment: Yard been quiet so far this year and she finished well held on her AW comeback
runners_data.spotlight: Six-race career can be split into two contrasting halves, namely steady progress in maidens and steady regress in handicaps; hence a turnaround is required.

runners_data.name: White Ladder
runners_data.note: Only natural front-runner gives him tactical advantage, 40-1 third last time suggests ability
runners_data.comment: Improved for nurseries/cheekpieces last summer; up in trip/no headgear on stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Seven-race maiden; belied his 40-1 odds with 1l third upped to 7f at Salisbury (good) on stable/seasonal debut; possibilities off same mark back down in grade, provided he builds on that effort.

runners_data.name: Blossom In The Air
runners_data.note: Low weight compensates for poor form, but fading pattern suggests distance concerns
runners_data.comment: Makes her stable/handicap debut after 167 days off; cheekpieces on; much more needed
runners_data.spotlight: Showed no improvement at Lingfield (6f) on stable/handicap/seasonal debut and remains far from solid in form terms.

runners_data.name: Superstorm
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up runner whose style needs others to go fast early, solid recent placings
runners_data.comment: Placed in both starts since being gelded but well beaten in his two starts on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Nine-race maiden whose consistent 7f form includes making the frame in all three outings this term, latest at Lingfield (good) returned to turf from AW; solid contender who is in the mix.

runners_data.name: Molly Mac
runners_data.note: 177 days off track is major concern despite previous consistent form, returning from long break
runners_data.comment: Not threat to front pair when third here on stable debut (7f); tries a new trip today
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in four of her last five 2yo starts but seems rather exposed and is the only runner in this field who lacks recent match practice; makes stable/seasonal debut.

runners_data.name: Inclusive
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits if pace develops, first-time cheekpieces suggest connections expect improvement
runners_data.comment: Third at Southwell on New Year's Day, but twice well held since; look elsewhere
runners_data.spotlight: Inconsistent maiden who has been beaten about 8l in each of her two starts for this yard; first-time cheekpieces need to make a difference.

runners_data.name: Wild Rosie
runners_data.note: Another hold-up runner who needs pace to aim at, breeding suggests trip will suit
runners_data.comment: Stable/handicap/seasonal debut offered little encouragement last month; cheekpieces go on
runners_data.spotlight: Five-race maiden; faded into sixth of 13 in first-time cheekpieces at Newmarket (1m) most recently; bred to do better still, being related to two winners for her connections; possibilities dropped back in trip.

runners_data.name: Shining Guest
runners_data.note: Weak form profile but low weight and handicap debut could see improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Thrice-raced filly who has very weak form claims, having beaten a total of only one rival; on the positive side, she may fare better now handicapping with 6f reappearance under her belt.

runners_data.name: Bear Steps
runners_data.note: Poor recent form but first-time headgear suggests stable expects better, needs gear to work
runners_data.comment: Well held in three starts in novice/maiden company; makes her turf/handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Showed no improvement switched to handicap level last time, finishing midfield, and still has RPRs in the 30s; chance depends on the effects of first-time headgear.

runners_data.name: Accommodation
runners_data.note: Dismal last run over extended trip, better at shorter but still weak claims
runners_data.spotlight: Modest third in final AW attempt and ran dismally (last of 14) upped to 1m at Windsor on handicap/turf debut since; best watched unless the market suggests a bigger effort is likely.

runners_data.name: Jooliah
runners_data.note: Poor form over various trips, 5lb claiming apprentice the only positive
runners_data.comment: No impact in four starts last year; big improvement required back from seven months off
runners_data.spotlight: Five-race maiden who has a poor chance on bare figures achieved mostly over 6f; gives 7f another go.

races.paceDynamic: White Ladder is the only confirmed front-runner in this 15-runner field, meaning he can dictate terms without pressure and set a sustainable pace from the front. Multiple prominent runners like Pennine Way, Komodo Rose, Blindfold Games, and Miss Starlet will track closely but none are natural pace-setters. This creates a moderate gallop through the middle sections before the field bunches up entering the home straight. The uncontested lead and manageable fractions heavily favour front-runners and prominent racers who can position early without energy expenditure.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: White Ladder Controls
scenarios.trigger: If White Ladder breaks cleanly and dictates an uncontested lead
scenarios.body: He sets comfortable fractions while prominent runners like Pennine Way and Komoda Rose sit perfectly placed just behind. The lack of early pace pressure allows these forward-positioned horses to kick clear in the final furlong while hold-up horses find too much traffic in a bunched finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent runners press White Ladder early creating stronger fractions
scenarios.body: The increased pace sets up perfectly for closer Superstorm and Wild Rosie who can sit off the stronger gallop. White Ladder and other pace angles weaken in the final furlong as the hold-up horses find their finishing kick more effective.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Messy Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If White Ladder fails to break cleanly or gets headed early by prominent runners
scenarios.body: A stop-start pace develops with no clear leader, creating a bunched field turning for home. The tactical speed and positioning of experienced runners like Miss Starlet and Blindfold Games proves decisive in a rough-and-tumble finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Longshot Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the market leaders fail to handle the soft ground or race shape
scenarios.body: Lesser-fancied runners with solid recent form like Molly Mac returning from a break or Superstorm continuing his consistent run find themselves in perfect position. The competitive handicap nature allows an improver to capitalize on the favorites' shortcomings.

watchPoints.text: White Ladder's early positioning is crucial - if he misses the break or gets headed early, the entire pace dynamic changes
Watch for any market support for Bear Steps or Inclusive as first-time headgear could signal stable confidence
Molly Mac's fitness after 177 days off will be evident early - any signs of rustiness rule her out
The large field size means traffic problems likely for hold-up horses like Jungle Knight and Wild Rosie
Soft ground conditions favor those with proven form on similar surfaces, limiting several runners' chances

runners_data.spotlight: Has won on soft and gained his fifth success when winning at Lingfield (5f, good) 22 days ago, making it four wins from his last four starts on turf; steps back up to 6f and he's a contender off this 5lb higher mark.

runners_data.name: Mart
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who should be handy early but hasn't won for over a year and faces a tough task off this mark
runners_data.comment: There have been some good efforts in his losing run of 16, though not of late
runners_data.spotlight: Seven wins from 47 starts, the most recent success coming at Lingfield (6f, good) last May off an 11lb higher mark; respectable effort when fourth of 12 at Redcar (6f, good to firm) 15 days ago and now needs to build on that.

runners_data.name: Elvetham
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing blinkers who is unproven on ground slower than good, which poses a significant concern here
runners_data.comment: Scored in added blinkers at Lingfield (6f AW) in April; similar efforts (on RPRs) since.
runners_data.spotlight: Unproven on ground slower than good; justified market support when winning in first-time blinkers at Lingfield (6f, AW) in April and has finished third in each of his three starts since, most recently at Thirsk (6f, good) five days ago; solid chance if handling conditions.

runners_data.name: Alafdhal

runners_data.name: Albert Cee

runners_data.spotlight: Didn't get home over 7f at Southwell in March and appreciated the drop to 6f when winning there 20 days ago following a short break; both wins on turf have been on good to soft, and has claims off this 3lb higher mark.

runners_data.name: Court Drive
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who hasn't won on turf for over a year and struggled when last seen at Wolverhampton 36 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win on turf came on good to firm at Pontefract last August off 4lb higher; had to switch for a run and couldn't finish strongly enough when last of six at Wolverhampton 36 days ago but shaped as if in form; however, others make a bit more appeal.

runners_data.name: Court Of Session
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with soft ground form who broke his turf duck at Nottingham just seven days ago and arrives in good heart
runners_data.comment: Won readily over 6f on Wednesday and this move back up in trip will suit; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Five-time AW winner who belatedly opened his account on turf when coming from off the pace to win at Nottingham (6f, good) a week ago; has form on ground slower than good and has to be respected under a 4lb penalty.

runners_data.name: Skellig Isle
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who is completely unraced on soft ground, making her ground suitability a major unknown

runners_data.name: Big Bard
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has won twice on soft but returns after 63 days off and trainer is 0 from 29 in the last 14 days
runners_data.spotlight: Two of his five wins on turf have been on soft; came back to form when winning at Kempton (6f, AW) in January but he's been well beaten in both starts since; a 63-day break needs to have done him good.

runners_data.name: Kyoto
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer making his turf debut having shown encouragement in handicaps on the all-weather recently
runners_data.comment: Showed ability in three starts at Lingfield; open to improvement on handicap/Tapeta debut
runners_data.spotlight: 0-4 but did shape with some encouragement at Southwell (6f, AW) on his handicap debut 20 days ago after being held up from his wide stall; makes his turf debut and he's open to progress.

races.paceDynamic: Albert Cee looks the lone confirmed front-runner in this field, with prominent runners Mart and Alafdhal likely to press him early but neither guaranteed to force a strong gallop. The majority of this field are hold-up horses (Silky Robin, Elvetham, Court Drive, Court Of Session, Skellig Isle, Big Bard, Kyoto) who will be looking to come from off the pace. With Albert Cee likely to get an uncontested lead on the soft ground over 6f, he can dictate a steady tempo before quickening. This race shape strongly favours the front-runner and any prominent racers who can avoid the inevitable traffic problems that will develop behind them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Albert Cee Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Albert Cee gets an uncontested lead and dictates the tempo from the front.
scenarios.body: He can string out the field at his own pace and prove hard to peg back when the closers make their moves in the final furlong. The soft ground will blunt the finishing kick of the hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Behind
scenarios.trigger: If the large group of hold-up horses get bunched up and struggle for racing room in the straight.
scenarios.body: Several of the better horses will find themselves short of room when they need it most, allowing a smoother traveller to capitalise. The winner will come from those who avoid the scrimmaging.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Early Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Albert Cee goes too slow early and gets swamped by the field turning for home.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where the hold-up horses with the best turn of foot can unleash late. Silky Robin and Court Of Session, both recent winners, could benefit most.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Press Forward
scenarios.trigger: If Mart or Alafdhal decide to take the race to Albert Cee from the start.
scenarios.body: A stronger early gallop develops which could set up the race for the closers, but the soft ground may still favour those racing prominently. The pace-setters tire and get picked off late.

watchPoints.text: Albert Cee must be watched closely in the betting - if his price contracts sharply it suggests connections are confident about his front-running tactics working
Monitor the early pace development as Mart and Alafdhal could disrupt Albert Cee's plan if they go forward aggressively from the start
Watch for traffic problems in the straight as seven hold-up horses will be looking for gaps simultaneously in the final two furlongs
Keep an eye on Elvetham's market support as any confidence would be concerning given his unproven status on soft ground
Observe Silky Robin's positioning early as his recent form suggests he could be the best of the closers if getting a clear run

races.paceDynamic: Daaris is the only confirmed front runner in this field, meaning he can dictate terms without pressure through the early stages. With all other runners showing hold-up tendencies, there will be a bunched field tracking behind as Daaris sets a sustainable gallop over this stamina-testing 1m6f trip on soft ground. The lack of pace pressure will create a tactical affair where the tempo may be modest until the final 3f, when the field compresses and it becomes a sprint finish. This race shape strongly favours those with a strong finishing kick who can produce their best effort late, making hold-up horses with proven soft ground form the profiles to follow.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Daaris Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Daaris maintains his lead without serious challenge until the straight
scenarios.body: The lack of pace pressure allows him to conserve energy and kick clear when the field comes to him. His recent AW wins show he has the tactical speed to respond when challenged, and soft ground suits his running style.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Catches Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the field closes rapidly in the final 2f and Daaris ties up
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop on testing ground finds out Daaris's stamina reserves, allowing strong finishers to sweep past. Horses with proven soft ground form and finishing kicks benefit from the pace collapse.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Suits Closer
scenarios.trigger: If Daaris sets a steady tempo and the race becomes a sprint from 3f out
scenarios.body: The tactical nature rewards horses who can quicken sharply rather than stay strongly, turning it into more of a speed test. Those with recent form and lighter weights can capitalise on the compressed finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Daaris Fades Early
scenarios.trigger: If Daaris doesn't handle the soft ground or distance and drops back before the straight
scenarios.body: Without the leader to aim at, the race becomes messy with no obvious pace, suiting versatile performers who can adapt. The race fragments and rewards horses who can find their own rhythm.

watchPoints.text: High Favour hasn't run for 75 days and has shown a pattern of fading in the finish, making him a risky proposition over this stamina-testing trip
Watch if Daaris actually goes forward early or sits closer than expected, as his hold-up style rating contradicts being the only pace angle
Smokey Malone was too keen last time and his poor turf record suggests he may not adapt to the surface switch from his recent AW success
Several trainers including Kevin Frost and Gary Moore are struggling with poor 14-day strike rates, potentially impacting their runners' readiness
The soft ground conditions favour Beggarman and Dissident based on their historical performance on similar surfaces

runners_data.note: Course specialist with three wins here but 10lb higher than last local success
runners_data.comment: Good second over C&D last September and could improve for last month's reappearance run
runners_data.spotlight: Won three times here last year (good to soft/good to firm), the most recent coming over C&D off a 10lb lower mark than today's; eighth in both starts since returning from a 182-day break and better is needed.

runners_data.name: Advancing
runners_data.note: Prominent runner better on AW, needs to prove turf effectiveness off this mark
runners_data.comment: Not particularly solid kept to turf and others are preferred
runners_data.spotlight: All three of his wins have been on the AW, the most recent at Kempton (1m) in March off 4lb lower; never a threat when sixth at Windsor (1m, good to firm) 16 days ago and he was well beaten on soft ground last year.

runners_data.name: Padua
runners_data.note: Can race freely but 307-day absence after making all unsuccessfully at Sandown
runners_data.spotlight: Can race freely, just as he did when making all at Haydock (7f, good) last summer; didn't get away with it at Sandown (7f, good) 307 days ago and he's since been gelded; tongue-tie is removed and he needs to settling better now stepping back up in trip on his reappearance.

runners_data.name: Renewal
runners_data.note: Prominent type who failed to beat a rival on handicap return at Lingfield 10 days ago
runners_data.comment: Unexposed 4yo who could have a big part to play back down to 1m on her reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Record of 4232 in novice/maiden events and ran well when second of 12 on her handicap debut at Newcastle (1m2f, AW) in October; however, she failed to beat a rival home at Thirsk (1m) on her reappearance and needs to take a big step forward from that effort.

runners_data.name: Bella Perla
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse dropping in grade but failed to beat a rival in two turf starts recently
runners_data.comment: Better for step up to 1m on AW in 2025, winning two of three; might need this for new yard
runners_data.spotlight: Won a maiden at Southwell (7f, AW) and two 1m handicaps at Lingfield (AW) last year when trained by the Crisfords; drops in grade having failed to beat a rival home on her stable debut at Ascot (1m, good) 32 days ago and has a bit to prove on turf.

runners_data.name: Where's Freddy
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist placed twice over course and distance including on soft ground
runners_data.comment: Inconsistent last term but some good course form; possible player on his reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: All three wins on turf have been on the Newmarket July course (7f/1m) but he has been placed in two of his three starts over this C&D, including on soft; never featured on his reappearance 25 days ago and needs to build on that.

runners_data.name: Carron
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse better on AW with poor recent turf form including last of five at Newcastle
runners_data.spotlight: Made it 3-4 on the AW when winning at Newcastle (1m, AW) in March but below that level in two starts on turf since, including when last of his group of five at Newmarket (1m; first-time cheekpieces) 39 days ago; cheekpieces discarded.

races.paceDynamic: Sprightly Dance is the only confirmed front runner and will be allowed to dictate a sustainable pace without pressure. Percival and Advancing are likely to track just behind as prominent runners, but neither has pace-pressing tendencies. With most of the field comprised of hold-up horses including Cavolo Nero, Mythical Guest, and Where's Freddy, the tempo will be modest through the early stages before quickening from the 3f marker. This controlled pace scenario strongly favours the prominent runners and those with tactical speed who can position close to the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Lead Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Sprightly Dance maintains his recent Wolverhampton form and gets soft splits in the straight
scenarios.body: The lack of pace pressure allows him to save energy for a sustained kick, while the hold-up brigade faces traffic problems in the sprint home. His 196-day break is concerning but Varian's 0/9 recent record reflects small sample size rather than poor form.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Percival shows his Saint-Cloud heavy ground form and Advancing finds improved turf form
scenarios.body: The duo can track the leader without pressure then out-kick him in the final 2f, with Percival's class edge and Advancing's recent race fitness proving decisive. The hold-up horses struggle to make up ground on the testing surface.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Charges
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is even slower than expected and Cavolo Nero gets a clean run through
scenarios.body: His proven 1m ability and recent placed form gives him the stamina edge in a slowly-run contest that becomes a sprint. Ferguson's horses are running well and the 46-day gap is ideal.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Course Specialist Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Gorgeous Mr George can overcome his 10lb ratings rise through superior course knowledge
scenarios.body: His three wins here last year prove he handles the track perfectly, and Gordon's 25% strike rate with Cunha horses adds tactical value. The 9lb weight advantage becomes crucial in a tight finish.

watchPoints.text: Sprightly Dance must handle the 196-day layoff after his Chelmsford disappointment to justify pace advantage
Percival's fitness after 87 days off and that tailed-off final run for Fabre needs monitoring early
Where's Freddy has strong course form and could outrun odds if getting the patient ride his style requires
Traffic problems likely in straight with nine hold-up horses needing room simultaneously
Ground conditions favoring those with proven soft/heavy form like Percival and Mythical Guest

races.name: attheraces.com/ascot Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Shaws Phoenix
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning to turf but poor AW form this season suggests limited claims despite suitable style
runners_data.comment: 0-16 and well held on stable debut/return at Southwell in April; others appeal more
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden who may benefit from the return to turf but otherwise has poor claims on her AW efforts this season for new stable.

runners_data.name: Al Baahy
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with solid classified form on AW, effective on turf and well-suited to this tactical scenario
runners_data.comment: 7yo who has been well held in his last three runs and sole turf win was in May 2023
runners_data.spotlight: Record is only 3-51 but he has form figures of 311 in classified events (all on AW); effective on turf; interesting back at this level.

runners_data.name: Nicely Curved
runners_data.note: Prominent type but maiden with contrasting recent efforts makes assessment difficult after 105-day break
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden whose Flat form for current yard comprises contrasting efforts in two Lingfield AW classified events; not sure what to expect.

runners_data.name: Heer's Sadie
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who is a three-time course winner, particularly effective here with proven venue form
runners_data.comment: All six wins at either Brighton or Yarmouth; handles most conditions but may need this
runners_data.spotlight: Three-time course winner, including last June/July; could go well returned to this venue with Lingfield reappearance under her belt.

runners_data.name: Girls Allowed
runners_data.note: Prominent 3yo improving after seasonal reappearance fourth, carried 11lbs less weight advantage
runners_data.comment: Soundly beaten thus far; makes handicap debut off lowly mark but improvement is necessary
runners_data.spotlight: Showed improvement with fourth-place finish at Leicester (7f) on handicap/seasonal debut; possibilities if building on that effort.

runners_data.name: Contemplation
runners_data.note: Hold-up style benefits from distance drop to 1m after recent longer-trip efforts, 7lb claimer reduces weight
runners_data.comment: Hasn't threatened in three runs for new yard, taking record to 0-7
runners_data.spotlight: Seven-race maiden whose last two efforts (1m2f) suggest this return to 1m will suit; otherwise has weak claims on overall form.

runners_data.name: Very Demure
runners_data.note: Likely front-runner whose penultimate C&D second in handicap represents solid form reference with cheekpieces retained
runners_data.comment: First turf start when second over 1m at Yarmouth in cheekpieces latest; claims
runners_data.spotlight: Seven-race maiden who is interesting on her penultimate effort, namely good second in C&D handicap when wearing first-time cheekpieces and just in front of Lady Of Clover on worse terms; now blinkered.

runners_data.name: Lady Of Clover
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner in excellent form after recent classified win, handicapper positive with 5lb weight rise
runners_data.comment: Placed in two of her three starts in 0-55 handicaps including over C&D; much respected
runners_data.spotlight: In-form 3yo who ran well over C&D on penultimate start, then opened her account in Wolverhampton classified contest (8.5f, AW) last week; may improve further at this level; respected even with 6lb penalty.

runners_data.name: Desert Charm
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who won division of this race last year on good going, reappearance effort encouraging over inadequate trip
runners_data.comment: Sole win came in a classified event last June; isn't sure to be suited by drop back to 7f
runners_data.spotlight: Record is just 1-9 but she gained the win in a division of this race last year (good); ran encouragingly over an inadequate 7f at Southwell (AW) on reappearance; major contender returned to this scenario.

runners_data.name: Harry Don't Bite
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but 77-day break and turf switch from moderate AW form creates uncertainty
runners_data.spotlight: Not particularly solid on his AW form (five starts); chance largely depends on the effects of this switch to turf.

runners_data.name: Lowestoft
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner showing improved stable debut form but needs to prove AW improvement transfers to turf
runners_data.comment: No closer than sixth in five starts; tongue-tie on for stable debut; hard to fancy
runners_data.spotlight: Improved AW effort when fourth in Southwell handicap (7f) on stable debut last time; needs to prove he can transfer the form to turf.

runners_data.name: Caitlin G
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with tendency to fade, first-time hood and distance increase needed to overcome poor recent form
runners_data.comment: Has failed to beat a rival in all four starts; look elsewhere
runners_data.spotlight: Poor claims on her form over shorter; combination of new trip and first-time hood needs to make a difference.

runners_data.name: Rockafeller Skank
runners_data.note: Hold-up 2yo with poor debut form, 222-day break and gelding operation since provide slim hope of improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Finished last in three runs last autumn; gelded since; the market signals may help to ascertain whether improvement is likely.

races.paceDynamic: Very Demure appears the only confirmed front-runner in this field, with most runners adopting hold-up or prominent tactics. Shaws Phoenix and Girls Allowed may press from prominent positions, but the overall pace will be modest and sustainable early. The lack of genuine speed horses creates a tactical race where positioning becomes crucial, with the final 2f likely to see a cavalry charge of hold-up horses including Al Baahy, Desert Charm, and Lady Of Clover. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can quicken late, as they'll face minimal early pace pressure and get optimal conditions to unleash their finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Brigade Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays genuinely slow early allowing closers to get into the race
scenarios.body: The lack of early speed means hold-up horses get perfect conditions to wind up their finishes, with Al Baahy and Desert Charm ideally positioned to strike late. Lady Of Clover's recent win gives her confidence to deliver another strong finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Speed Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Very Demure gets an uncontested lead and sustains the gallop throughout
scenarios.body: With no genuine pace pressure, Very Demure could dictate terms and prove hard to catch if maintaining her penultimate effort level. The lack of early speed horses means she faces minimal pressure until the final 2f.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tactical Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Shaws Phoenix and Girls Allowed engage Very Demure early creating genuine pace
scenarios.body: This forces a stronger gallop that could set up the race for a different type of finisher, potentially suiting Desert Charm's proven course form. The increased pace would compromise the pure hold-up horses' finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Surprise Package
scenarios.trigger: If the modest pace allows an improver like Contemplation or Lowestoft to get competitive
scenarios.body: The tactical nature and lack of standout form could create opportunities for horses showing recent signs of progress. Contemplation's distance drop or Lowestoft's stable debut improvement might prove decisive in a slowly-run affair.

watchPoints.text: Very Demure's early position will be crucial - if she gets a soft lead without pressure she becomes very dangerous
Lady Of Clover carries a 5lb penalty for her recent win which could prove decisive in a tight finish
Al Baahy has been away 25 days and trainer Kevin Frost is 0/15 in last 14 days, market support would be significant
Desert Charm drops to 7f at Southwell last time was inadequate, but needs to prove 1m effectiveness on return
Contemplation gets valuable 7lb weight allowance from claiming rider which improves her chances significantly
